mathematical_checks: Irrationality and zero mean give uniqueness. A polynomial lower bound on the divisors preserves rapid Fourier decay and constructs an actual smooth inverse.

Single complex Fourier characters give necessity of the Sobolev loss criterion; weighted square summation gives sufficiency for every real r. The D_s and Q_s conditions are equivalent and retain the critical endpoint.

If all polynomial bounds fail, the chosen increasingly sparse frequencies and coefficients produce one fixed smooth forcing. Every possible solution would have unbounded Fourier coefficients. This bridges the quantifiers rather than merely producing a different bad mode for each estimate.
The quadratic conjugate bound gives D_1>0 for sqrt(2)-1. Pell frequencies rule out every nonnegative loss below 1, so the minimum is attained.
m+4 integrations by parts and one power of small-divisor growth leave a summable cubic decay in two dimensions. The requested C^m estimate follows for every m>=0 without claiming four is optimal.

The optional irrationality-exponent classification is correct. The rubric accepts equivalent arithmetic criteria, short correct Fourier and closed-graph routes, and stronger valid estimates; it does not require the author's optional constructions.
